sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c68c7405eb127717.title: Aggravation
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c68c7405eb127717.description:
Aggravation is a board game where the point is to bring your chips back to home base after going around the game board. This game uses ASCII graphics to display the game board and allows for up to four players to play in turn. Up to three of these players can be controlled by the computer.

After rolling a six or one a player may place one of their four chips on to the game board and try to traverse it and head back home to a safe base. Landing on another player will mean that that player must take that chip back and restart with it by rolling a one or six. Rolling a six allows the player to roll again and players may not jump over other chips of their own. Therefore although named Aggravation this game, unlike the board game of the same name, plays and looks more like the board game Sorry.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cd730622ef4e4a88.title: The Alchemy Game
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cd730622ef4e4a88.description: Here is the basic principe of gameplay: on the playing field there are four icons for the "primary elements": water, air, earth and fire. When two elements merge, new objects, substances and physical phenomena are obtained (you can even make a thunderstorm, not to mention electricity and other such things). Thus, connecting together many different elements, you practically carry out the process of the formation of the world and evolution (only in schematic form). The game has tricks: sometimes you need more than two components to create a reaction; in many cases, one object can be obtained in different ways; not every combination of elements will give a result; some simple substances can break down into "primary elements" from a certain effect. There is a lot of combinations, and figuring them out is the goal of the game.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c2c3368948be7f07.title: Animal Math
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c2c3368948be7f07.description:
Animal Math is an educational game that uses pictures of animals to teach counting, sequences, addition and subtraction. For example, you choose addition and have to complete eight sums. When you have completed the eight correctly the game displays the congratulations screen with a fun little tune and then you move onto more difficult equations.

Aimed at junior school age children the game is simple enough for them to use. The text and pictures are big and easy to read.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c502b7cdbe1c9484.title: The Asian Challenge
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c502b7cdbe1c9484.description:
The Asian Challenge is an educational game which aims to improve the understanding of the Asian culture and geography. It was developed to be used during geography class. The player takes the role of a special investigator of the Senate Foreign Aid Committee who is tasked to travel around Asia and collect information.

Each time the player enters a new area, the text is divided into three parts: a short description of the country (including some historical and social information), optionally a list of items which the player can interact with and a list of available exits. Every country is only represented with a few screens. Besides not getting lost (the author recommends to use an atlas), the puzzles involve collecting items and using them in other places. The parser understands simple verb-noun constructions and a few single-letter abbreviations. At the end of the game, the player has to take a multiple-choice test which asks for information given during play.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c86d5487c2ae47e6.title: Avenger
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c86d5487c2ae47e6.description: Avenger is a shareware shoot 'em up arcade style game from Finland for one or two players and which is a bit of a cross between Galaxian and Space Invaders. The game starts in the year 2254 with a cut-scene showing the space station Finlanda and her escort vessel in the Alpha Centauri system. A horde of mysterious ships appear from nowhere and, after a short battle, the escort vessel is destroyed. The player takes the role of a pilot returning to the space station after a holiday. They find the station is now a base to many strange ships which attack their vessel.The object of the game is to achieve a high score. Gameplay is very much in the Space Invaders style. In the single player mode the left / right cursor keys being used to move the player's ship from side to side while the Right Alt key fires the main weapon and the Right Ctrl key fires a secondary weapon. The enemy ships, however, attack in the style of the enemies in Galaxian, swooping around the screen as they attack.The game maintains a high score table and has two modes of play, normal and challenge. Two-player action is side by side with both players sharing the keyboard. The challenge mode is only available in the full registered version which has 55 levels.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c117aa4d4708fcb5.title: Battle Fleet
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c117aa4d4708fcb5.description: Battle Fleet is a Battleship clone wherein you must place your five naval vessels on a grid while your computer or friend via modem does the same. After all the ships are placed you can now take turns trying to determine the location of each other's fleet and sinking them by taking well thought-out shots at the enemy grid. If you've placed a hit you will be notified of it on your enemy grid and can now try and guess which way the enemy ship is placed and sink them. Hence, the rules of the game are identical to the Milton Bradley game. The only differences are the grid numbering and some ship names.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c524ec49e53e1cbb.title: Commander Keen 9: Battle of the Brains
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c524ec49e53e1cbb.description:
Battle of the Brains, also known as Keen 9, is the third and final episode of the unofficial "The Universe is Toast" trilogy by Ceilick, with the bulk of the modding done by Ceilick, Mink and Tulip, with extensive patching by Levellass and Lemm. Work on the mod began shortly after the release of Dead in the Desert in 2009. It was released in February 2011.

The story continues where Dead in the Desert left off. After escaping the planet Calidune and being reuinted with his friends in the Bean-with-Bacon Megarocket, Commander Keen learns of Mortimer McMire's plans to destroy a giant star and incinerating the universe. He also learns that Mortimer has a space station containing several transporters which can be used to teleport to distant worlds and locations. One of these transporters is heavily guarded and believed to lead to Mortimer himself. Keen must travel to four different worlds in order to activate the controls which unlock the doors to the final teleporter so that he can stop Mortimer before the universe is toast!

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0ca95b82753fe3c43.title: Crime Lab: Case of the Missing Masterpiece
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0ca95b82753fe3c43.description: Crime Lab: Case Of The Missing Masterpiece is a very short, shareware, educational single player game focused on the forensic procedure of blood typing.The Acme Art Gallery was burgled on April 1st, 1988 and the thief made off with a valuable painting, hence the title. As a crime lab technician the player's job is to analyse a blood sample. After quite a few detailed screens explaining the principles of the science behind this process the player prepares two reference samples and a sample taken from the crime scene. Based on the results of their analysis they then choose from a suspect list whose blood types are known.The game is keyboard controlled, has no sound and can be replayed because the culprit changes.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cee24ab62eb389fa.title: Desert Race
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cee24ab62eb389fa.description:
Desert Race holds the possible distinction of being the first (and only?) animated driving game programmed entirely as a DOS batch file.  This implies all the expected limitations - system commands only, no real graphics/hardware access, and the absence of most useful programming constructs.  Nevertheless, it manages to implement a top-down car race in ASCII graphics, albeit without real-time continuous play (the game waits for a keypress before advancing to the next frame).

There's even a story, in which you set forth on a brutal race for survival in a post-apocalyptic Mad Max-style scenario.  The game takes place at night, and so only a section of the road is visible, fading to black at the edges; your only controls are moving left and right to switch lanes, trying to avoid incoming cars as they emerge from the darkness.  Colliding with a car (or with the edge of the road) will permanently extinguish your road rage.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c1a6819f1f0eff5f.title: Kubix
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c1a6819f1f0eff5f.description: Spanish puzzle game, divided into several levels. In the central part of the screen there are 9 or 16 creatures or objects (angry workers, helmets with eyes, blue gears, anthropomorphic hammers and wrenches), put in the form of a 3x3 or 4x4 square; on either of the four sides of this grid there are three or four pipes, that is, one for each row and column. The control is carried out by the mouse cursor, which by default has the shape of a "vertical" screwdriver with a pink handle. When you put it up to the pipe, the color of the latter changes to green (and if the structure is horizontal, the tool assumes a "lying" position). At the top right is the image of the latter, in which all the figures are arranged in a certain way, and the task at each level is to repeat this alignment on the playing field. This is achieved by clicking on the pipe ends, as a result of which the figures in a row or column are shifted by one position in the corresponding direction.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c069479a5a406639.title: Masque Solitaire Antics
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c069479a5a406639.description:
Masque Solitaire Antics is a compilation of single player card games that was later added to and released as Solitaire Antics Deluxe .

The collection contains the following solitaire games; Royal Family, Ant's Solitaire, Aces Out, Aces Up, Agnes, Auld Lang Syne, Calculation, Canfield, Carpet, Chamelion, Demon, Double or Quits, Easthaven, Fascination, Fortune's Favor, Golf, Klondike, Simplicity, Storehouse, Thumb and Pouch and Yukon.
Each game has its own help screen which explains the rules, and can be played in three levels of difficulty: normal, easier or harder.

When loaded the game will start at a random game which the player can either play or choose another game from the collections menu. All card games are played using the mouse.

At some points during the game, notably when a game ends, an animated ant appears on-screen.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cd0e650cfa6ba05d.title: Missile Attack
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cd0e650cfa6ba05d.description: The goal of the game is to protect the city from a missile attack. This will have to be done with the help of air defense missiles: each fired anti-missile creates a cloud of fragments which destroys the enemy missiles. You get 12 anti-missile missiles to defend against each attack, and you need to protect 12 buildings. It is especially critical to cover the central structure since it has a  radar: if you lose it, the mouse cursor disappears. You can, of course, continue to play without it but it becomes much more difficult. However, even if you did not save all 12 buildings but scored 1500 points, you will move to another city (there are 10 cities in the game). You will also have to deal with night attacks, when the location of the homing missiles can only be judged by small patches of light.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cc09d5efb6220a74.title: Prison Amok
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0cc09d5efb6220a74.description: Very simple bloody game. Prisoners are trying to escape and we need to shoot them with a revolver. A hit to the head instantly kills the prisoner, a shot to the legs slows him down, and the shot arms and legs completely immobilize the victim. In addition to the revolver, you can take a machine gun and a grenade launcher, but their ammunition is limited. The game has no division into levels or a logical end - the number of people running just increases over time.

This game is an epic adventure surrounding humanity in space. It has a combination of role-playing character building, team combat strategy, customizable spaceship combat, and adventure game exploration. Fly through space and explore the surfaces and bases of a few planets to unravel the mystery that's disturbing the known universe.

Most of the travelling is 2D, but the indoor corridors are 3D. The game features Paragraph books, where characters mention a paragraph number and you have to read from the booklet instead of getting the text in game. This functions as copy protection, making the game require guesswork to complete without the manual.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c4b508063a632ca9.title: Torus
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c4b508063a632ca9.description: A remarkable puzzle in a somewhat similar vein as Tetris. On top of the screen fall multicolored rings (four colors in total), three in a row; beneath them is a similar number of cylinders capable of holding a stack of six rings. Our task is to prevent the complete filling of any of them. To do this, at the bottom of the screen is a skull that we control, on which you can fit up to three rings and move them in such a way as to position three in a row - then they will disappear, turning into glasses. There is no division into levels, but over time the game speed increases.

sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c2b1fff59cbe46ef.title: Ulysses and the Golden Fleece
sha256-dos-manifest-v1:0c2b1fff59cbe46ef.description:
Ulysses and the Golden Fleece is an adventure game where you play the part of Ulysses in ancient Greece. The king has given you the task of finding the golden fleece, a legendary treasure which is protected by the gods. You begin your quest in a small town, and will need to travel to several far away lands to find the fleece. Many characters from ancient mythology will be encountered along the way, including King Neptune, the Sirens, Cyclops, and others. You need to find a way past them as well as the many obstacles on sea and land if you are to be successful.

Along the bottom of the screen is a text parser which accepts two word commands to interact with the game, and at the top (covering most of the screen) are graphics depicting your current situation. If needed, the graphics can temporarily be cleared to see some of the most recent commands entered.
